notes:
VERDICT DRIFT, headline finding: option-field ids are NOT carried over from the source case — they are silently rewritten to the destination project's DEFAULT custom-values block, even when the source used a different, equally-live block for the same field. TC-54489 (source) carries the upper block (case_type 318626, priority 318618, status 318632). Its existing copy TC-54490 carries the lower/default block instead (case_type 318599, priority 318591, status 318605) — verified again independently on TC-54502 (1985215), the copy created by this run's own experiment 2, which shows the identical lower-block substitution (case_type 318599, priority 318591, status 318605). This is reproducible across two independently created copies and is a real data-fidelity defect for any workspace where the source and destination use different custom-values blocks for the same logical option — the copy quietly ends up with a DIFFERENT priority/status/case than the case it was copied from, with zero signal that a substitution happened.

What DID copy correctly: (1) steps — copied with a brand-new step-row id (12372586 on the source vs 12372588 on TC-54490) and no shared_step_id/shared_step_detail_id on either side, so there is no aliasing between a case and its copy; the only oddity is that the copy's step row carries a populated hashed_id where the source's was null (a generation-time artifact, not a bug). (2) template_id/template_name/template_step_type — fully preserved on the copy (1164 / 'Test Case Steps' / 'test_case_steps' identical on source and copy); this capability does NOT have edit_test_case's silent-template-reset bug. (3) tags — preserved verbatim (['mcp-probe'] on both TC-54489 and TC-54490). NOT tested: custom_fields — both source and copy report [], so nothing here demonstrates preservation either way; do not read this as confirmed-preserved.

Folder-count accuracy (asked for explicitly): VERIFIED ACCURATE. Folder 765811's own record reports cases_count:2 (direct) and total_cases_count:3; list_folder_test_cases on the same folder returns exactly 2 rows (TC-54490, TC-54491); its one subfolder (765817) independently reports cases_count:1, total_cases_count:1, which reconciles 2+1=3 exactly. No drift found in folder counts in this probe.

Priority-2 experiment 1 (copy to a nonexistent destination_folder_id): a clean, if uninformative, 400 {success:false} with no message and no async marker — the destination folder is pre-validated before any copy work starts, exactly as describeCapability's guidance claims. Confirmed nothing was created anywhere (source folder 764138 re-read afterward: 23 rows, unchanged). This is DIFFERENT from create_bulk_test_cases, which the task notes silently discards a bogus folder id and files the case into the path folder instead, 200, no signal — bulk_copy_test_cases does the safer thing here.

Priority-2 experiment 2 (one valid id + one nonexistent id): SILENT HALF-SUCCESS UNDER 200. The call returned success:true and copied only the valid id (1985023 → new case TC-54502, integer id 1985215, filed into folder 765817 as requested); the nonexistent id (999999999) was dropped with absolutely no trace — no skipped-ids field, no message, no count-mismatch warning anywhere in the body. The only way to notice anything happened to only one of the two requested ids is external: folder 765817's cases_count went from 1 (before, per setup step 4) to 2 (per this response's own cases_count:{'765817':2}), i.e. exactly one case landed, not two. This settles the three-way question the task posed: of 'silent half-success under 200' / 'undeclared 502' / 'clean named rejection', it is the first — the same silent-discard failure mode as create_bulk_test_cases's bad-folder-id case, just applied to a bad case id instead.

Contract drift (200 schema): the declared success schema lists source_path_folders as a REQUIRED field. Neither successful call captured in this probe (the previous agents' straight copy, nor this run's experiment 2) ever returns it — the live 200 body has destination_path_folders (as declared) but no source_path_folders at all, and instead returns an undeclared folders key not present in the schema. Shallowest missing path: source_path_folders (top level).
